own_delta_para: THIS KEEPER'S OWN DELTA (miso-159): MISO's thermal fleet is no longer uniformly stamped vintage 2010. The ERCOT-only master plant registry misses every MISO plant, and _commission_year's hardcoded 2010 fall-through had made the entire age-escalation limb of THERMAL_AVAILABILITY inert — 108.70 GW carried as 13-15 years old when the fleet's true cap-weighted vintages run 1976.8 (ST_GAS) to 2006.5 (CC_REGULAR). The new zero-DOF boolean routes the fall-through through the measured capacity-weighted EIA-860 COD map (the same single source that already drives the monthly online mask), removing 2.9 GW of phantom annual capability and 1.6 GW of phantom summer capability in 2025, concentrated in COAL / CT_PEAKER / ST_GAS — the classes that set MISO's summer and shoulder prices. Against a same-HEAD zero-delta control the repair lifts demand-weighted prices +1.97/+2.82/+2.93% (direction disclosed in advance; not claimed as skill), takes C3a to -0.1/-5.4/-13.1% (2023 at essentially zero error; 2025 still failing at -13.1%), and FLIPS C3b-2025 back through its 0.200 gate (0.212 -> 0.200 exactly — knife-edge, reported as such), recovering the shape regression the miso-148 promotion accepted. market_story: COAL — MISO's coal fleet is the oldest large block on the system (true cap-weighted vintage 1982, 33 GW past the age-40 escalation onset): a 43-year-old steamer carries a measurably higher forced-outage rate and a deeper performance derate than its nameplate suggests, so the real market has ~1.3 GW less coal capability in an average hour than a uniformly-young fleet would — the mid-merit coal the model was dispatching in those hours is, in reality, in the shop. ST_GAS — the 1976-vintage gas steamers are the fleet's most fragile class (age ~48, every MW past both onsets); their real availability is lower everywhere, which is part of why the real overnight/shoulder stack is thinner than the model's was. CT_PEAKER — the summer price-setter: the real CT fleet averages 26 years old with 85% of its capacity past the escalation onset, so on a July afternoon the real market has ~0.5 GW less peaking capability than a 15-year-old fleet would offer — the real supply curve runs out of cheap capability sooner, and the marginal unit sits higher up the stack, which is exactly the direction of MISO's observed summer prices. CC_REGULAR — mostly 2000s-vintage and barely past onset; the repair moves it least (+0.1 GW), consistent with CCs being the fleet's healthiest class in reality.
